transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Welcome in—what brings you here today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, is it okay if I sit here? Okay, great. 

Well, I guess what brings me in is... my sleep has just gotten a little, um, messed up lately. I'm sure it's probably not a huge deal, but... I'll either stay up half the night with my mind just kind of running, or I end up waking up way too early and I just feel like I never really rested at all. I really try to push through it for my bookkeeping job, but... I don't know. 

I mean, is that a normal thing to come in for? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
Aside from the trouble sleeping, do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things during the day, and having a hard time controlling that worry?

Um... no, I don't really think so. I mean, I care about my work and want to make sure all my accounts balance out, but I wouldn't call it excessive worry. And I can usually control my thoughts just fine during the day when I'm focusing on my spreadsheets and things. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just... I don't feel like my mind is spinning with worries during the daytime, really. Does that make sense? Is it alright if I just have the sleep issues without the daytime worry part?
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed your mood feeling down, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Um, well... I guess I have been feeling a little down, maybe? I mean, I hate to complain because I know I have a good job and I worked really hard to get my own condo and everything, but... lately, I just wake up with this heavy, almost empty feeling. 

Sometimes just sitting in my living room makes me want to cry, which is silly, I know. I should be happy with what I have, right? I try not to let it show, but... yes, I guess my mood has been a bit lower than usual. Is it normal to feel that way even when things on the outside seem fine? I hope I'm explaining this right.
You mentioned feeling down and empty—how many days or weeks would you say you've been feeling this way?

Um... well, I guess it's been a little while. I hope it's not awful to admit this, but... it's probably been about five months? 

It's just this kind of... depressed, guilty fog that's been hanging around. I mean, I know I shouldn't feel that way, especially because it actually got a lot worse right after I finally bought my condo. Which sounds so ungrateful of me, right? I really should be thrilled about having my own place. But yeah, about five months of that feeling. 

Is... is it okay that I waited that long before coming in to see someone? I just kept hoping I would do a better job of snapping out of it on my own so I wouldn't have to bother anyone with it.
Over these past several months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even when your schedule allows time for them?

Um... I guess so, yeah. I mean, I used to really love going to my salsa class, but I just... I stopped going a while ago. I know I should go back, it's good exercise and everything, but I just haven't had the energy. 

And... well, I used to paint a little bit. Nothing professional, just for fun. But my paints have just been sitting out on the table for months now. I look at them and I just feel... nothing. It's almost like they belong to somebody else. 

I feel so bad about it, like I'm just being lazy or wasting the things I used to care about. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person? I really do want to enjoy those things again, I just... I don't know how right now. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

Before these past five months, would you say you generally felt like your usual self, or has this low, empty mood been a pattern you've dealt with off and on for a much longer time—like a year or more?

Um, well... I guess I've always been a little bit up and down? But not exactly like this. I mean, before these last five months, I think I was mostly doing okay. 

I don't think it's been a pattern for a whole year or anything like that. I really try to keep a good attitude most of the time, you know? I don't want to be someone who's just always sad or complaining. So, yeah, I think before I bought the condo, I was pretty much my usual self. 

I hope it's okay that I can't remember exactly every single day from back then? But I'm pretty sure this really heavy, empty feeling is just from the last few months. Does that make sense?
During these past several months of feeling down, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off not being here?

Um... no, no, I haven't. I mean, I know sometimes people who feel depressed think about things like that, but I would never want to do anything to hurt myself. 

I just... I feel really bad and empty, like I said, but I'm not... I'm not thinking about ending things or anything scary like that. I know how much that would hurt my family and my friends, and I really wouldn't want to be a burden to them in that way. 

I just want to figure out how to feel better and be helpful again. I hope you don't think I'm... you know, that bad off? I'm really trying my best to keep it together.

Would you say these feelings and low energy have made it noticeably harder for you to keep up with your bookkeeping work and daily responsibilities, or have you mostly been able to manage them despite how you're feeling?

Um... well, I'm still going to work every day. I really try to be reliable, you know? But... I guess it has been a little harder lately. 

I've been making some mistakes with the reconciliations. Nothing terrible, I don't think! But my supervisor did pull me aside to ask if everything was okay. I felt so awful about it. I really hate letting people down or causing extra work for anyone else. 

And, like I mentioned before, I haven't been going to salsa class, and I've kind of been avoiding my friends a bit. I just... I don't feel like myself, and I don't want to bring everyone else's mood down when they're trying to have a good time. 

I'm really trying to push through it and do my job, though. I hope that's okay? I mean, I'm still managing the basics, mostly. Is that the kind of information you need?
Over these past several months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight—either eating more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Um... I guess my appetite has been a little bit off? Nothing too extreme, I promise. I just... I haven't really felt like eating big meals lately. 

Sometimes I'll end up skipping dinner, or I'll just sit at my table eating some crackers while I try to sort out my budget notebook. I know I should be eating better, and I really am trying to make sure I eat something every day so I don't get sick or anything. 

I did notice the other day that my work pants are feeling a little looser than they did a few weeks ago. So I guess I might have lost a little bit of weight without meaning to. I hope that's not too concerning? I'll definitely try to make an effort to eat more regular meals if you think I need to. I want to make sure I'm taking care of myself the right way.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy most days, or having trouble concentrating on tasks like your bookkeeping?

Um... yeah, I guess I have been a little more tired than usual. I really try to get a good night's sleep so I can be ready for work, but... even when I'm in bed all night, getting going in the morning is just really hard right now. 

Like, just walking from the parking lot into the office... it feels like I'm dragging sandbags or something. I know that sounds silly, and I'm really trying not to complain! It's just... it takes so much effort. 

And then with the bookkeeping... I want to do a good job, I really do, but by lunchtime, my brain just feels so worn out. It's like I can't focus the way I usually do. I'm still getting my work done, though! I promise I'm not just sitting there doing nothing. I just have to read things a few extra times to make sure I don't mess up. 

Is it normal to feel that worn out when you're feeling down? I hope I'm not just being lazy... I really am trying my best to stay on top of everything.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a discrete, ~5-month episode of depressed/empty mood, anhedonia (loss of interest in salsa and painting), insomnia (initial and early morning awakening), decreased appetite with unintentional weight loss, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and mild functional impairment (work errors, social withdrawal) without prior chronic low-grade mood disturbance, psychotic features, or suicidal ideation. This clinical picture meets criteria for a single major depressive episode of moderate severity (functional impairment present but core activities maintained), rather than mild (F32.0), severe (F32.2), dysthymia (F34.1), or GAD given explicit denial of excessive, uncontrollable daytime worry.
